questions: Do you have a history of Parkinson's disease?
Do you experience difficulty initiating movement, such as when getting out of a chair or starting to walk?
Do you feel that your steps become shorter and faster once you start walking (a sensation known as festination)?
Do you tend to lean forward when standing or walking?
Do you have trouble turning around while walking without losing your balance?
orders: Perform the Romberg test (standing with feet together, eyes open then closed)
Assess for retropulsion by pulling on the patient's shoulders while they stand
Evaluate for paratonia (gegenhalten) in the upper extremities during passive movement
Check for primitive reflexes (glabellar tap, snout, palmomental, grasp)
Order an MRI of the brain to evaluate for hydrocephalus and white matter changes
results: 1. Perform the Romberg test (standing with feet together, eyes open then closed)
Romberg test, repeated with distraction: negative
2. Assess for retropulsion by pulling on the patient's shoulders while they stand
3. Evaluate for paratonia (gegenhalten) in the upper extremities during passive movement
muscle tone (spasticity, rigidity, paratonia): normal; no dystonic head posture, no sensory trick
4. Check for primitive reflexes (glabellar tap, snout, palmomental, grasp)
5. Order an MRI of the brain to evaluate for hydrocephalus and white matter changes
